subject.title: Echo contamination: stripInboundMetadata not called in outbound delivery pipeline

question: Should this issue be closed only after the direct outbound delivery sanitizer lands, or should maintainers require the broader trusted inbound-decoration contract before considering the leak fixed?
rationale: Current source still has the direct outbound gap, but related work raises a real security-boundary concern about forgeable text sentinels versus a trusted marker contract.

options.title: Land the direct safety net first
options.body: Repair, review, or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/50520 so normal outbound delivery stops leaking metadata, and track the trusted-marker work separately.

options.title: Fold closure into trusted contract
options.body: Treat this issue as blocked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95333 only if that PR also proves the normal outbound delivery path no longer leaks metadata.

options.title: Require live Discord proof before closure
options.body: Keep the issue open until a repaired branch demonstrates before/after Discord delivery behavior in both thread and non-thread group contexts.

recommendation.title: Land the direct safety net first
recommendation.body: Repair, review, or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/50520 so normal outbound delivery stops leaking metadata, and track the trusted-marker work separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The central outbound payload normalization plan history makes this the closest owner boundary for the direct fix path.
